title: Multi-institutional grading of Barrett's esophagus dysplasia without stain normalization using a pathology foundation model and multiple instance learning
abstract: arXiv:2611.26562v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Barrett's esophagus dysplasia grading suffers substantial inter-observer variability, particularly for low-grade dysplasia, complicating clinical decision-making. We conducted a retrospective multi-institutional diagnostic accuracy study of a foundation model-based deep learning system for dysplasia grading, using 969 H\&E-stained whole slide images from four institutions. Patch-level classifiers trained on expert annotations identified diagnostically relevant regions, followed by attribute-aware multiple instance learning for slide-level classification as non-dysplastic Barrett's esophagus (NDBE), low-grade dysplasia, or high-grade dysplasia. On a held-out test set (n = 130), macro-averaged AUC was 0.96 (95\% CI 0.93--0.98). For binary dysplasia detection, sensitivity was 98\% (80/82) and specificity 81\% (39/48), with a negative likelihood ratio of 0.030 and quadratic-weighted \kap{} of 0.83 against expert consensus. tldr: 该研究构建了基于病理学基础模型与属性感知多示例学习的深度学习系统，在无需染色归一化的条件下，利用四个机构969张全切片实现了巴雷特食管异型增生的高精度自动分级（AUC达0.96，与专家共识高度一致）。
en_tdlr: This study developed a deep learning system combining a pathology foundation model with attribute-aware multiple instance learning, achieving high-accuracy multi-institutional grading of Barrett's esophagus dysplasia without stain normalization (macro-averaged AUC of 0.96 and strong agreement with expert consensus).
